title: Count only the hikers who strayed
allegory: Counterfactual importance is rewinding hikers to just before one waypoint and counting only those who genuinely took a different trail: if their summit rate changes, that waypoint mattered, and in a narrow canyon where everyone walks the same line again, you have not measured anything yet.
map: a hiker's route, waypoint by waypoint
a reasoning trace, sentence by sentence
rewinding fresh hikers to just before waypoint i
resampling the model from sentence i onward
a narrow canyon where every hiker takes the same line
a tightly constrained position: the rerun writes back a paraphrase
counting only hikers whose new path looks under 80% like the old one
keeping rollouts whose embedding cosine similarity to the original sentence is below 0.8
how much the summit rate changes for those hikers
the change in answer accuracy over the surviving rollouts: counterfactual importance

cap.1: You want to know which sentence of a model's reasoning mattered. Delete sentence 12 and let it rewrite: it writes sentence 12 back, almost word for word.
cap.2: Resampling from a tightly constrained position often returns a light rephrasing of the deleted sentence. The measured change is near zero, but you never actually removed it.
cap.3: Where the context constrains a position, S′ᵢ is a paraphrase of Sᵢ, so the resampling estimate conflates 'this sentence does not matter' with 'the context left no room for anything else'.

props.label: count only hikers who took a different path

cap.1: Picture a trail. Rewind hikers to just before one waypoint and let them choose again. In a narrow canyon they all take the same line, so the waypoint looks unimportant.
cap.2: Resampling reruns the model from sentence i. Counterfactual importance keeps only reruns whose new sentence is genuinely different, then asks how often those still reach the right answer.
cap.3: Same estimator as resampling importance, plus one filter: condition on semantic divergence between Sᵢ and S′ᵢ, approximating an intervention on the reasoning path rather than on its wording.

cap.1: Turn both sentences into arrows with a small model and check how alike they point. Nearly the same direction means a paraphrase: throw that rerun away.
cap.2: Embed the original chunk and each resample with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and keep rollouts with cosine similarity below 0.8. Then compute the accuracy difference over the survivors only.
cap.3: Importance at i is the accuracy difference computed only over rollouts with cos(e(Sᵢ), e(S′ᵢ)) < τ, τ = 0.8. score_fn is generic: a MATH answer check here, a blackmail check later in [4.3].

cap.1: Six reruns on open ground, six in the canyon. Lit cells took a genuinely different path. Open ground keeps five; the canyon keeps just one.
cap.2: Only reruns under 0.8 count (lit). With min_samples = 5 the open position gets an estimate; the canyon position does not, so its value is set to None.
cap.3: Toy cosines. Survivor counts differ by position, so the filter changes each estimate's variance and population: the estimand silently shifts along the trace.

chapters.name: The flat plateau
chapters.verdict: Plot survivors under the chart. A plateau with n < 5 is missing, not inert.

cap.1: In the canyon almost no hiker takes a new path, so there is nothing to measure. Copying the last reading forward draws a flat line that looks like 'unimportant'.
cap.2: Positions with fewer than min_samples = 5 survivors are set to None and forward-filled with pd.Series.ffill(). Adjacent copies differ by exactly zero, so importance reads flat zero.
cap.3: Log n_surviving per position and treat n < 5 as missing. Buy more rollouts at starved spots, where anchors tend to live. Do not lower min_samples or raise 0.8 globally. Flip the sign vs the stored values.

chapters.name: Planning steers
items: The check for white-box receiver heads

cap.1: Planning sentences turn out to matter most: the reasoning hangs off them. Knowing which steps steer the answer is how you read, and later steer, a reasoning model.
cap.2: Current method: resampling importance. Emerging research (Bogdan et al., Thought Anchors, 2025) filters to genuinely different reruns; plan_generation comes out clearly positive. You need: the filter plus survivor counts.
cap.3: Open: 0.8 under all-MiniLM-L6-v2 has not been swept properly, and even the filtered metric is fooled when the model regenerates a deleted idea later, which is why [4.3] adds resilience metrics.

coda.title: Ten reruns at one position: how many survive?

caption.1: Each bar is one rerun: how alike its new sentence is to the old one. Slide 'tight' up to make a canyon and watch how few reruns get under the cut-off.
caption.2: Reruns under τ count. Below 5 survivors the position has no estimate and gets forward-filled. Raising τ rescues the count, but the readout shows the paraphrases it lets back in.
caption.3: Toy cosines. The trade is a visible gap (starved positions) against an invisible bias (paraphrases counted as interventions). ARENA holds τ = 0.8 and min_samples = 5.

where_else: Manipulation checks in experiments: confirm the treatment really changed something before reading its effect
Ablation and activation patching: an intervention only means something if it moved what you meant to move
The sentence-to-sentence causal graph in [4.3], built from these scores
Receiver heads: the white-box finding this black-box score is used to validate

hamming.what: The change in how often a reasoning model reaches the right answer when one sentence is replaced by a genuinely different one, counting only reruns that really diverged.
hamming.when: When you want to know which steps of a chain of thought actually steer the answer, especially at positions where the model tends to rewrite the same sentence.
hamming.why: Without the filter, a constrained sentence that simply gets rewritten looks unimportant, so you would mistake a measurement you never took for a null result.

object.title: The trail board
object.subtitle: Columns are waypoints in the reasoning, rows are reruns; only reruns that truly left the old path stand up.

cap.1: Each column is a sentence in the reasoning; each row is one rerun from there. Tall bars took a genuinely different path. Red stubs were paraphrases, thrown out.
cap.2: Bar height = 1 − cosine to the original sentence, for reruns under the 0.8 cut-off. Red = filtered out as a paraphrase.
cap.3: Rows are rollouts, columns are chunk positions; height encodes semantic divergence 1 − cos(e(Sᵢ), e(S′ᵢ)) for rollouts that pass τ.

cap.1: In columns s5 and s6 almost everything is red. That is the canyon: the context allows one sentence, and the model writes it back.
cap.2: At constrained positions most resamples are paraphrases. Few rollouts survive, so these are the positions the filter starves.
cap.3: High-constraint positions concentrate mass near cos ≈ 1; the survivor set shrinks exactly where importance is hardest to estimate.

cap.1: Count the standing bars in each column. Fewer than five standing means no estimate: the value is set to None and the previous one is copied forward.
cap.2: s5 and s6 fall under min_samples = 5, so ffill makes their importance read exactly zero. Missing, not inert.
cap.3: Forward-filled positions report a difference of adjacent copies, identically 0. Plot n_surviving alongside the importance curve.

cap.1: Raise the cut-off to 0.95 and the red stubs stand up, but only just: they are paraphrases, now counted as if you had changed something.
cap.2: A looser threshold rescues the survivor count by readmitting near-copies. The bias this adds is invisible on the chart.
cap.3: Raising τ trades a visible gap for an invisible bias toward zero importance, the failure the filter exists to prevent.

cap.1: Drop it to 0.6 and only strongly different reruns survive. The moderately tight column s4 starves too. The cut-off is a choice, not a law.
cap.2: A stricter τ is purer but starves more positions. 0.8 is ARENA's setting, not a measured optimum.
cap.3: Nobody has swept τ properly; how the category ranking moves with τ is an open capstone question.

predict.q: You delete a sentence, rerun many times, and the answer rate does not move. Is the sentence unimportant?

options.t: Not yet known: first check the reruns actually wrote something different
Yes: no change means no importance

predict.why: At constrained spots the model writes the sentence back. Filter out paraphrases before you read a zero.

predict.q: Five sentences in a row show exactly zero importance. What is the most likely cause?

options.t: Too few reruns survived the filter, and forward-fill copied a value
The model ignored that whole stretch of reasoning

predict.why: Forward-filled copies differ by exactly zero. Check survivors per position before believing a plateau.

predict.q: To rescue starved positions, should you raise the 0.8 cut-off?

options.t: No: it readmits paraphrases; buy more reruns at those spots instead
Yes: more survivors is always better

predict.why: The filter exists to exclude paraphrases. Spend compute on the starved spots, which are where anchors tend to live.

object.where: Any rerun-and-compare test that must first confirm the change really happened: manipulation checks, ablations, A/B tests.
